主要内容: In 2016, the wearable technology market is expected to see a significant boost with the introduction of 'smart clothes' that can stretch with the user's movements. Angelo Zino, a senior industry analyst at S&P Capital IQ, predicts that a slew of smart clothing will be introduced in 2016. Companies like Alphabet, Samsung, and Intel are working on technology for smart clothing, which would allow wearers to monitor heart rate, steps, and time spent sitting. Google's Project Jacquard enables the embedding of hardware into fabric using standard industrial looms, allowing users to connect to apps or phone functions through their clothing. Samsung showcased its Smart Suit and Body Compass workout gear at CES 2016, while Intel's Intel Curie chip, which measures movement and acceleration, is expected to be embedded into clothing. DuPont has also developed stretchable 'electronic ink' for machine-washable smart garments. OMsignal's smart bra, which can record physical activity data and transmit it to an iOS device, is set to launch in the spring. Analysts believe that while the market for smart clothes may be limited, there is significant upside potential, with garments expected to make up 10 percent of the wearable-device market in the next five years.
